clips.send: A friend sends this to whoever says 'the experts would tell us if it was bad for us': the cold case of tobacco executives testifying under oath that smoking was safe while sitting on their own data proving otherwise - anger at being told a flat lie for decades.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau on tobacco's own paper trail.

His claim: by the 1950s, tobacco companies had internal research linking smoking to serious disease - and sat on it. Their own executives later testified under oath to Congress that smoking wasn't linked to any illness at all.

Decades on, some finally admitted it on record: they'd had the data the whole time, and stayed quiet because of what admitting it would cost them in lawsuits.

His point: executives, politicians and media all repeated the same line, and most who repeated it never checked it themselves.

What's one thing you were told was safe that wasn't?

clips.send: A friend sends this to the one who just bought a stronger deodorant: the surprising reason a smell can mean something is building up inside, not just on the skin - mild anxiety about what's really going on in your body.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau on the real reason you might still smell, even after showering.

His point: a stronger deodorant just covers the smell, it doesn't ask why it's there. A smell researcher's own work found body odor varies by diet and region - what you eat changes how you smell, not just how much you sweat.

His claim: today's worst body odor isn't the natural kind every person has. It's coming from the toxins and poisons already built up in your body.

Cover it up, or find out what's really loading up inside you?

clips.send: A friend sends this to the one who just bought a fourth deodorant brand: the gross, impossible-to-ignore detail about what one colon held onto for decades, and what Kevin says that smell is actually telling you - disgust mixed with real worry.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau's blunt read on body odor: if you stink, you're toxic.

His claim: a bowel movement that reeks means waste has been sitting in your colon far too long, not that it's normal. He points to stories from colon-cleansing facilities, including a claim that John Wayne carried 18 pounds of impacted waste in his colon, some of it for decades.

People who do a colon cleanse report a flatter stomach, more energy, less bloating - and less body odor, because the toxin load driving the smell is gone.

His view: that smell is a symptom, and symptoms left alone tend to catch up with you.

What is your body trying to tell you?
